# The Rememberers

**Type:** Paladin order (Oath of Remembrance)
**Patronage:** None — self-founded, self-sustained
**Territory:** Scattered across the Severed Lands; members operate independently
**Size:** ~30 sworn Rememberers, plus aspirants

## Overview

The Rememberers are an order of paladins bound by the Oath of Remembrance: to witness every loss, shield the displaced, carry the names of the dead, and smite those who prey on the already-broken. They are not a church. They are not an army. They are a network of sworn protectors, each of whom adopts a Riftborn community or individual as their ward.

The order was founded by a Riftborn paladin whose name has been deliberately forgotten — the Rememberers believe that their founder's identity is less important than their mission. What's known: the founder was among the first wave of Riftborn arrivals, swore the oath at a dead Anchor Door, and spent the rest of their life protecting other new arrivals. When they died, others took up the oath. The chain has never broken.

## The Ledgers

Every Rememberer carries a ledger — a small, hand-bound book that contains names. The names of Riftborn they've protected. The names of Riftborn who've died. The names of home worlds that may no longer exist. The names of people who asked to be remembered and people who couldn't ask anymore.

Reciting the names is part of the Rememberer's daily ritual. It takes hours for some — decades of names, page after page. The ritual is not about grief. It's about witness. The Rememberers believe that a person isn't truly gone until no one remembers them. As long as one Rememberer still recites their name, they're not forgotten. They're not done.

When a Rememberer dies, their ledger is passed to their successor. Some ledgers contain centuries of names — passed down through generations of Rememberers who never met each other but share the same book, the same oath, the same burden.

## Structure

The Rememberers have no central authority. There is no high priest, no grand master, no headquarters. Each Rememberer operates independently, choosing their own wards, swearing their own oaths. What binds them is the code:

- **Witness.** Acknowledge every loss. When a Riftborn speaks of what they lost — a world, a family, a name — the Rememberer listens. They write it down. They remember.
- **Shield.** Protect those who have already lost too much. A Rememberer's ward is under their protection. Threats to the ward are met with force.
- **Remember.** Carry the names. The ledgers are sacred. Losing a ledger is the only crime the Rememberers recognize as unforgivable.
- **Smite.** Those who exploit, hunt, or prey on the displaced receive no quarter. The oath does not negotiate.

Rememberers recognize each other by their ledgers — worn, handled, carried in a specific way. When two Rememberers meet, they exchange names: one from each ledger, offered like a gift. It's the closest thing the order has to a greeting.

## Notable Rememberers

- **Brother Ash:** The oldest active Rememberer. Ash has been carrying his ledger for forty years — it's thick as a brick, pages yellowed and soft. He protects the Warrens, specifically the newest arrivals who haven't learned the Warrens' rules yet. He's a familiar sight in the Warrens' narrow streets — an old man in battered armor, writing names in a book, never far from someone who needs him.
- **Sister Candle:** A young Rememberer who took the oath after her entire Riftborn community was wiped out by a riftbeast pack. She was the only survivor. Her ledger starts with their names — all thirty-seven of them. She's been tracking the pack ever since. She says she'll stop when her ledger is full. She says it's almost full.
- **The Silent:** A Rememberer whose name is unknown because they took a vow of silence — not as penance, but as witness. They believe that if they stop speaking, they can hear the names better. The Silent communicates through writing. Their ledger is written in a script no one can read, but when they recite — silently, lips moving — the effect is the same.

## Relationship to Other Factions

- **Returners:** Natural allies. Many Rememberers protect Returner communities. V respects the Rememberers but finds their methods impractical — individual protection doesn't scale. A Rememberer can save one Riftborn. The Returners want to save all of them.
- **Thornwall Council:** Tolerated. Rememberers in Thornwall are registered as religious pilgrims, which gives them legal standing without requiring the council to endorse them. The council finds them useful — a Rememberer in the Warrens keeps the peace in ways the guard can't.
- **The Anchor Church:** Overlapping but distinct. The Church reveres the Doors as sacred. The Rememberers revere memory as sacred. They collaborate when their missions align. They don't compete — there's too much work for either to claim exclusivity.

## Hooks

- Brother Ash's ledger has been stolen — taken from his quarters while he was responding to a Warrens disturbance. The thief left a note: "One name for every Door fragment the Returners have hidden." Ash won't ask the Returners to pay the ransom. He's preparing to get the ledger back himself.
- Sister Candle found the pack — the riftbeasts that killed her community. They're denning in the Verdant Margin, near an Anchor Clearing. She's asking for help. She's not asking for mercy — for the riftbeasts or for herself.
- A Rememberer's body was found near a dead Anchor Door. Their ledger was open beside them. Every name in it had been crossed out — not by the Rememberer. The handwriting is wrong.
